proposal.summary: FileReplicationPro 7.5.0 installs files and directories under 'C:\Program Files\FileReplicationPro' with 'Everyone' full control, allowing replacement of the service binary prunsrv.exe (service 'frp' running as LocalSystem) for privilege escalation. The etc\properties.xml file contains a SHA-1(base64) password hash that can be modified to gain web interface access.
proposal.cwe_quote:
Incorrect file/folder permissions in Diasoft Corporation's File Replication Pro 7.5.0 allow privilege escalation by
replacing a file with another one that will be executed with "LocalSystem" rights from Windows Services application.

AV.quote:
Incorrect file/folder permissions in Diasoft Corporation's File Replication Pro 7.5.0 allow privilege escalation by

proposal.recommended_next_step: Confirm and reproduce by verifying ACLs on the installation directory, attempting to replace prunsrv.exe and observing service execution as LocalSystem; if confirmed, advise vendor to set restrictive ACLs (remove 'Everyone' full control), protect service binary and config files, and rotate credentials/hashes stored in properties.xml.

evidence_quotes.claim: Directory permissions showing Everyone Full Control
Service runs as LocalSystem and binary path
Description of exploitation by replacing prunsrv.exe
evidence_quotes.quote:
To exploit the vulnerability a malicious actor/process must weaponize or replace the prunsrv.exe executable that runs
with LocalSystem privileges as "frp" (FRPReplicationServer) service, since the application's path has "Everyone" full
access permissions.

evidence_quotes.claim: Properties.xml contains SHA-1(base64) hashed password which can be modified
evidence_quotes.quote:
the "properties.xml" file in the "etc" folder inside program's path contains the hashed password for remote
access stored in sha1(base64) value, that is possible to modify.
